- [Persistent sandboxes](https://docs.archil.com/compute/sandboxes/introduction.md): Run untrusted, AI-generated code in isolated Firecracker microVMs with persistent disks.
- [Sandbox images](https://docs.archil.com/compute/sandboxes/images.md): Start sandboxes from public or private OCI images and reuse prepared images.

- [Data Sources](https://docs.archil.com/concepts/data-sources.md): Configure bidirectional synchronization for Archil disks to existing data sets
- [Authorization](https://docs.archil.com/concepts/authorization.md): Configure who is authorized to access the Archil APIs or disk
- [Sharing Disks](https://docs.archil.com/concepts/sharing-disks.md): Archil disks can be shared between multiple servers simultaneously
- [Branches & Checkpoints](https://docs.archil.com/concepts/branches-and-checkpoints.md): Snapshot the state of an Archil disk and fork independent, writable copies from any snapshot.
- [Metering](https://docs.archil.com/concepts/metering.md): How Archil measures active data in the high-speed storage layer
- [S3 Object Storage](https://docs.archil.com/data-sources/s3-object-storage.md): Configure S3-compatible storage providers as data sources for your Archil disk
- [Architecture](https://docs.archil.com/details/architecture.md): Overview of Archil disk architecture
- [Security & Compliance](https://docs.archil.com/details/security.md): How Archil protects your data, and what we commit to contractually
- [Consistency](https://docs.archil.com/details/consistency.md): Understanding Archil&apos;s consistency model between clients and data sources
- [Application Compatibility](https://docs.archil.com/details/support.md): Archil is designed for full POSIX-compatibility
- [Performance](https://docs.archil.com/details/performance.md): Archil Performance Specifications
- [Performance tips](https://docs.archil.com/details/performance-tips.md): Practical ways to get the most out of an Archil disk.
- [Client caching](https://docs.archil.com/details/caching.md): How the Archil client caches data in memory, and the controls for warming, sizing, and refreshing it.
- [Solution Comparison](https://docs.archil.com/details/comparison.md): How Archil compares with EBS, EFS, and S3 FUSE adapters. Archil ran git, npm, and SQLite transaction workloads about 5x to 190x faster than Amazon EFS.
- [Best practices](https://docs.archil.com/administration/best-practices.md): Recommended ways to structure your Archil accounts, disks, and credentials for production and multi-tenant workloads.
- [Pricing & Billing](https://docs.archil.com/administration/billing.md): Plans, usage rates, monthly minimums, and billing for Archil
- [Organizations](https://docs.archil.com/administration/organizations.md): Use Organizations to effectively share disks between members of your team
- [S3 API](https://docs.archil.com/protocols/s3-api.md): Read and write Archil disks over an S3-compatible HTTP API — list, download, upload, and delete objects with any S3 client, no mount required.
- [TypeScript SDK](https://docs.archil.com/sdks/typescript.md): Programmatic access to Archil disks from TypeScript and Node.js applications
- [Python SDK](https://docs.archil.com/sdks/python.md): Programmatic access to Archil disks from Python scripts, CI, and notebooks
- [AI SDK](https://docs.archil.com/integrations/ai-sdk.md): Context your agent can understand
- [eve](https://docs.archil.com/integrations/eve.md): Context your agent can understand
- [just-bash](https://docs.archil.com/integrations/just-bash.md)
- [`archil` CLI](https://docs.archil.com/reference/archil-cli.md): Reference for the Linux system CLI that mounts Archil disks as local folders.
- [`disk` CLI](https://docs.archil.com/reference/disk-cli.md): Reference for the Node CLI that creates disks, runs `disk exec`, and manages API keys.
- [Terraform provider](https://docs.archil.com/reference/terraform.md): Manage Archil disks, users, and API tokens with Infrastructure as Code
- [Kubernetes CSI driver](https://docs.archil.com/reference/csi-driver.md): Documentation on mounting using the [Kubernetes Container Storage Interface](https://kubernetes-csi.github.io/docs/) (CSI) driver for Archil disks.
- [Uninstall tools](https://docs.archil.com/reference/uninstall.md): Remove the Archil client, the disk CLI, and the CSI driver.
- [Troubleshooting](https://docs.archil.com/reference/troubleshooting.md): Solutions to common issues with Archil disks
- [Region availability](https://docs.archil.com/reference/regions.md): Archil regions and availability
- [Bring Your Own Cloud (BYOC)](https://docs.archil.com/reference/byoc.md): Run the full Archil platform, fully managed by Archil, in your own cloud account or on bare metal.
- [Verify Linux downloads](https://docs.archil.com/reference/verify-linux-downloads.md): Verify the authenticity and integrity of an Archil Linux release before installing it.
- [Client Release Notes](https://docs.archil.com/reference/client-release-notes.md): Release history for the Archil client
- [Changelog](https://docs.archil.com/reference/changelog.md): History of updates to the Archil platform and client
- [Subprocessors](https://docs.archil.com/legal/subprocessors.md): Third parties Archil engages to process data on your behalf
- [API Reference](https://docs.archil.com/api-reference/introduction.md): Programmatic access to the Archil Control Plane
- [List Disks](https://docs.archil.com/api-reference/disks/list-disks.md): Returns all disks owned by the authenticated account.
- [Create Disk](https://docs.archil.com/api-reference/disks/create-disk.md): Creates a new disk with the specified configuration. A default disk token user is automatically generated and returned in the response, so the disk is immediately mountable. The one-time disk token appears in `authorizedUsers[].token` and cannot be retrieved again. (This disk token is scoped to the…
- [Get Disk](https://docs.archil.com/api-reference/disks/get-disk.md): Returns detailed information about a specific disk.
- [Delete Disk](https://docs.archil.com/api-reference/disks/delete-disk.md): Deletes a disk and all associated resources.
- [Create Share URL](https://docs.archil.com/api-reference/disks/create-share-url.md): Creates a signed, time-limited URL for downloading a file without authentication. The URL expires after 24 hours by default; pass `expiresIn` to set a custom lifetime up to 7 days.
- [Execute Command on Disk](https://docs.archil.com/api-reference/serverless-execution/exec-disk.md): Launches a Firecracker microVM with the specified disk mounted, runs the given command to completion, shuts down the microVM, and returns the command result.
- [Execute Command with Multiple Disks](https://docs.archil.com/api-reference/serverless-execution/exec-multi.md): Launches a Firecracker microVM with the supplied set of disks each mounted at its own relative path under `/mnt/archil`, runs the command to completion, and shuts down the microVM. Activation is atomic: every disk mounts or none of them do.
- [Search Files (grep)](https://docs.archil.com/api-reference/serverless-execution/grep-disk.md): Searches files under a directory on the disk for lines matching a regular expression. Listing and matching are fanned out across ephemeral exec microVMs, so the request finishes within the user's time budget regardless of the size of the directory.
- [List Sandboxes](https://docs.archil.com/api-reference/sandboxes/list-sandboxes.md): All the account's sandboxes, oldest first.
- [Create Sandbox](https://docs.archil.com/api-reference/sandboxes/create-sandbox.md): Provisions a sandbox VM with the requested shape and an internal, persistent Archil disk backing its root filesystem. This backing disk cannot be disabled or replaced with an existing disk. Use `mounts` to attach additional existing disks at guest paths; omit it or pass an empty list to create a san…
- [Get Sandbox](https://docs.archil.com/api-reference/sandboxes/get-sandbox.md)
- [Delete Sandbox](https://docs.archil.com/api-reference/sandboxes/delete-sandbox.md): Permanently deletes a stopped, exited, or failed sandbox and its backing disk. A sandbox with child forks cannot be deleted until those children are deleted, starting with the deepest ones.
- [Create Sandbox Connection](https://docs.archil.com/api-reference/sandboxes/create-sandbox-connection.md): Returns a short-lived WebSocket URL used by the sandbox process API. The URL contains a signed token that expires at `expires_at`; an open WebSocket can remain connected after the token expires.
- [Set Sandbox Timeouts](https://docs.archil.com/api-reference/sandboxes/set-sandbox-timeout.md): Replaces one or both sandbox timeout settings. Updating `timeout` while the sandbox is running resets its hard expiration deadline to that many seconds from now, capped at 24 hours after the current session started. Updating `idle_ttl_seconds` resets the idle countdown when no direct process connect…
- [List Sandbox Ports](https://docs.archil.com/api-reference/sandboxes/list-sandbox-ports.md): Lists the explicitly exposed public ports for the sandbox.
- [Expose Sandbox Port](https://docs.archil.com/api-reference/sandboxes/expose-sandbox-port.md): Creates or returns public access to a TCP port in the sandbox.
- [Unexpose Sandbox Port](https://docs.archil.com/api-reference/sandboxes/unexpose-sandbox-port.md): Removes an explicitly exposed public port. An enabled sandbox service publishing the same TCP port remains publicly reachable.
- [List Sandbox Port Tokens](https://docs.archil.com/api-reference/sandboxes/list-sandbox-port-tokens.md): Lists unexpired private port token metadata without returning raw tokens.
- [Create Sandbox Port Token](https://docs.archil.com/api-reference/sandboxes/create-sandbox-port-token.md): Creates token-authorized HTTP access to one port. Send the raw token returned by this request in the `X-Archil-Token` request header at the stable `<port>-<sandbox-route-id>.<zone>` hostname. Public ports accept connections without a token; otherwise a valid token for that sandbox and port is requir…
- [Get Sandbox Port Token](https://docs.archil.com/api-reference/sandboxes/get-sandbox-port-token.md): Returns token metadata without its raw token. Expired tokens return not found.
- [Delete Sandbox Port Token](https://docs.archil.com/api-reference/sandboxes/delete-sandbox-port-token.md): New private connections using the token fail after this request completes; established connections remain open. Expired tokens return not found.
- [Get Sandbox Network](https://docs.archil.com/api-reference/sandboxes/get-sandbox-network.md): Returns the last committed network policy for a running, paused, or stopped sandbox.
- [Update Sandbox Network](https://docs.archil.com/api-reference/sandboxes/update-sandbox-network.md): Applies the complete replacement policy to a running sandbox, then records it as the current policy. A rejected update leaves the previous policy unchanged. Free-plan accounts cannot update network policies and receive 403 with code sandbox_network_plan_required. For paid accounts, an empty object r…
- [Pause Sandbox](https://docs.archil.com/api-reference/sandboxes/pause-sandbox.md): Snapshot the CPU & memory state, then stop the VM. The sandbox reports `pausing` until the snapshot commit marker is durable and the VM exits, then reports `paused`. Attached process connections close, while agent-owned processes remain available for reattachment after resume. A sandbox that is stil…
- [Fork Sandbox](https://docs.archil.com/api-reference/sandboxes/fork-sandbox.md): Checkpoints a running source sandbox and creates an isolated writable disk branch. Forks from running or paused sources resume from the source's CPU, memory, and disk state. Forks from stopped sources cold-boot from the saved disk checkpoint. A running source is resumed after its checkpoint; paused…
- [Resume Sandbox](https://docs.archil.com/api-reference/sandboxes/resume-sandbox.md): Restores a paused sandbox's committed CPU and memory snapshot. Resuming a running sandbox or a pending resume is idempotent. Only a `paused` sandbox can begin a new resume; `stopped`, `exited`, `failed`, `stopping`, `pausing`, or a pending cold start returns 409.
- [Start Sandbox](https://docs.archil.com/api-reference/sandboxes/start-sandbox.md): Cold-boots from the persisted configuration and disks. If the sandbox was paused, its memory snapshot is consumed and discarded before the new VM runs; disk state remains. Without mount changes, starting a running sandbox or a pending cold start is idempotent. A sandbox that is stopping, pausing, or…
- [Stop Sandbox](https://docs.archil.com/api-reference/sandboxes/stop-sandbox.md): Gracefully shuts down the guest, then checkpoints its disk before entering `stopped`. The sandbox and any forks from it cold-boot from disk state. Stopping a paused sandbox reuses its existing disk checkpoint. In-flight processes receive the guest shutdown signal.
- [Build Image](https://docs.archil.com/api-reference/images/build-image.md): Builds an OCI image for use by sandboxes. Poll [Get Image](/api-reference/images/get-image) until it is `ready`, then pass its `image_id` when creating a sandbox.
- [Get Image](https://docs.archil.com/api-reference/images/get-image.md): Returns the image's build status and latest successful digest, if available. Failed builds include a `failure_reason`. Use [Build Image](/api-reference/images/build-image) (`POST /api/images`) to retry interrupted builds.
- [Add Disk User](https://docs.archil.com/api-reference/disk-users/add-user.md): Adds an authorized user to a disk. Users can authenticate via: - **token**: A shared token with a nickname and 4-character suffix - **awssts**: AWS STS role assumption with an IAM principal ARN
- [Remove Disk User](https://docs.archil.com/api-reference/disk-users/remove-user.md): Removes an authorized user from a disk.
- [List API Tokens](https://docs.archil.com/api-reference/tokens/list-tokens.md): Returns all API tokens for the authenticated account.
- [Create API Token](https://docs.archil.com/api-reference/tokens/create-token.md): Creates a new API token for programmatic access. The full token value is only returned once at creation time.
- [Delete API Token](https://docs.archil.com/api-reference/tokens/delete-token.md): Revokes and deletes an API token.
- [Get Usage](https://docs.archil.com/api-reference/billing/get-usage.md): Returns what the account's meters recorded over a window, for the window as a whole and per interval, in each meter's own unit (vCPU-hours, GiB-hours, GiB-months, calls) with no prices applied. Usage reaches billing once per reporter interval from every region, so an interval's figures can still gro…
- [Get Costs](https://docs.archil.com/api-reference/billing/get-costs.md): Returns the same usage as `/api/billing/usage` priced at the account's rates, for the window and per interval and meter, before the plan's included credits and base price: the cost of what was used, not what will be invoiced. Summed over the billing period it is the usage line of the invoice; `/api/…
- [Get Summary](https://docs.archil.com/api-reference/billing/get-summary.md): Returns a billing period's statement as a sum: `meteredCostCents`, the period's usage at the account's rates with a breakdown by meter; `adjustments`, the lines the plan applies (the included credits taken off, the base price added); and `billedCostCents`, what they come to, which is what the period…
- [Coding agent in a sandbox](https://docs.archil.com/guides/agents/coding-agent.md): Give an AI agent a persistent Linux sandbox where it can install packages, write code, and run a web app you can open.
- [Code interpreter](https://docs.archil.com/guides/agents/code-interpreter.md): Give an AI agent a stateful Python kernel in a persistent sandbox to analyze a public dataset, with results on an Archil disk.
- [Claude Code](https://docs.archil.com/guides/agents/claude-code.md): Run Claude Code headlessly in an Archil sandbox, with its workspace and session history on an Archil disk.
- [OpenCode](https://docs.archil.com/guides/agents/opencode.md): Run OpenCode headlessly in an Archil sandbox, with its workspace and session history on an Archil disk.
- [OpenAI Codex](https://docs.archil.com/guides/agents/codex.md): Run the OpenAI Codex CLI headlessly in an Archil sandbox, with its workspace and session history on an Archil disk.
- [Parallel agents](https://docs.archil.com/guides/agents/parallel-agents.md): Fork a prepared sandbox once per agent, let each agent try a different approach, and keep the fork with the best score.
- [Vector search with LanceDB](https://docs.archil.com/guides/agents/vector-search.md): Store a LanceDB table on an Archil disk, serve vector, filtered, and hybrid search from read-only replicas, and update it in place.
- [Analytics with DuckDB](https://docs.archil.com/guides/analytics/duckdb.md): Query 81 million places from the Overture Maps public bucket with DuckDB, without copying the data, and serve results over HTTPS.
- [Search logs across sandboxes](https://docs.archil.com/guides/analytics/log-search.md): Write structured logs from several sandboxes to one Archil disk, then search and aggregate them from your laptop.
- [Evals and RL environments](https://docs.archil.com/guides/training/rl-environments.md): Fork a task environment once per rollout, grade each agent run with a hidden grader, and collect the graded trajectories as a JSONL dataset on an Archil disk.
- [Host a web app](https://docs.archil.com/guides/apps/web-app.md): Run a Python web app with a SQLite database on an Archil disk, serve it at a public URL, and fork preview environments from a template.
- [PostgreSQL](https://docs.archil.com/guides/apps/postgres.md): Run PostgreSQL in a sandbox with its data directory on an Archil disk, and connect to it from your machine with psql.
- [MySQL](https://docs.archil.com/guides/apps/mysql.md): Run MySQL in a sandbox with its data directory on an Archil disk, and connect to it from your machine with the mysql client.
- [Modal](https://docs.archil.com/guides/platforms/modal.md): Mount an Archil disk in Modal Sandboxes so their files outlive the container.
- [E2B](https://docs.archil.com/guides/platforms/e2b.md): Mount an Archil disk in E2B sandboxes so their files outlive the sandbox.
- [Daytona](https://docs.archil.com/guides/platforms/daytona.md): Mount an Archil disk in Daytona sandboxes so their files outlive the sandbox.
- [Vercel Sandbox](https://docs.archil.com/guides/platforms/vercel-sandbox.md): Mount an Archil disk in a Vercel Sandbox so its files outlive the sandbox.
- [AWS Lambda MicroVMs](https://docs.archil.com/guides/platforms/lambda-microvms.md): Mount an Archil disk in an AWS Lambda MicroVM so its files outlive the MicroVM.
- [Troubleshooting mounts on other platforms](https://docs.archil.com/guides/platforms/troubleshooting.md): What happens when a sandbox goes away with an Archil disk mounted, how to release a stale lock, and notes for E2B, Daytona, Modal, and Vercel Sandbox.
